leftEvidence.title: Solomon’s vineyard is set beside the speaker’s own

points.label: Solomon-relative action
points.left: Solomon’s vineyard at Baal Hamon yields money through keepers, while the speaker claims direct possession of her own vineyard.
points.right: Solomon receives enormous gold, makes shields and a throne, acquires luxury goods, and multiplies chariots and imported horses.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The woman distinguishes what belongs to Solomon from what remains before her.
points.right: Merchants, kings, traders, and royal agents feed a concentrated display of wealth and power.

payload.posture: The Song contrasts royal vineyard revenue with a woman’s own vineyard; Kings inventories concentrated royal treasure and power.

rightEvidence.title: Gold, shields, throne, chariots, and horses accumulate

payload.tension: The lyric voice asserts possession beside the same king whose reign is known for accumulation.
payload.title: Solomon’s vineyard and Solomon’s accumulated wealth
